rv.q: Because Broadway has been hit by a wallop of fun — and an avalanche of confetti — courtesy of the preposterously enjoyable revival of “Much Ado About Nothing" that opened Thursday night at the Winter Garden Theatre.
This Much Ado About Nothing never lacks for giddy enchantment, from the Tony-worthy performances of stars Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell to the irresistible choreography...
And the performances by Ms. Atwell and Mr. Hiddleston are so radiant, funny and seductive that any attempt to resist them would be as foolish as it would be futile.
They deliver the language beautifully and complement it with vigorous action.
The mood in the room becomes almost too ecstatic to bear.
At the Winter Garden, all resistance is futile.
The Much Ado About Nothing he has directed, starring Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell, arrives on Broadway like a spitwad shot out of a confetti cannon.
Come for the superheroes, stay for the dance party.

Let me put that worry to rest: Much Ado About Nothing , Jamie Lloyd’s eye-popping pink confection, starring a deliciously paired Tom Hiddleston and Hayley Atwell as beloved bickerers Benedick and Beatrice, is the most fun you’ll have on Broadway this season.
Jamie Lloyd, known for his bold takes on revivals, directs this five-star production.
It’s undeniably entertaining, especially if you’re in the right mood.
This Benedick has so little to prove that his relaxed delivery turns the Bard’s iambic pentameter into something as easily digested as dialogue written by David Mamet or Stephen Adly Guirgis.
Hiddleston and Atwell nail the zesty, rapid-fire banter that makes “Much Ado” soar.

Even a semi-successful Lloyd joint, as this colorful, dance-filled take on William Shakespeare’s Much Ado About Nothing ultimately proves to be, is still far more invigorating than most contemporary Broadway spectacles.
Tom Hiddleston largely makes it work.
Lloyd’s production triumphs in silliness, always at its best when embracing full hearted, full-throated fun.
For all its fun, and sometimes to Lloyd’s frustration, this is also a play about what happens when two people ruthlessly committed to the bit finally have to grow up to get what they want.
And here he transforms the Bard's work into a virtual musical comedy that is contemporary, light on its feet, and irresistibly fun.
The result is a show that is perpetually aware of how entertaining it is supposed to be, sometimes at the expense of actually being entertaining.

cn.t: Critics largely embrace Jamie Lloyd's confetti-drenched, pop-infused revival, praising Hiddleston and Atwell's electric chemistry. Most find it irresistibly fun, though a few feel the sensory spectacle overshadows Shakespeare's emotional depth.

lo.t: Opens 12 AM day before performance, closes 3 PM day before. Winners drawn at 10 AM and 3 PM.
lo.inst: Winners notified by email and have five hours to claim and purchase tickets online. Limit 2 tickets.

vs.sum: The Winter Garden Theatre offers excellent legroom and spacious seating, making it one of the most comfortable venues on Broadway. Sightlines are generally good, though some side seats may have partial obstructions. The theater's ambiance is enhanced by its historical charm and garden-themed decor, while facilities are average with some potential for lines at restrooms.

acc.note: 20 wheelchair spaces (largest of Shubert theaters). 16 aisle transfer seats. Infrared devices available.
